lenses.refutation_attempt: The claim "deployed cue diffuseness is ~fully recoverable (floor~0) by content-blind re-organization" is structurally forced by a construction matched to the re-posing, not an empirical discovery. PROVEN: (1) exp07_core.reposed_companion is exactly global mean-centering: comp_reposed[m] = comp[m] - alpha*mu, mu = mean_m comp[m] (a single cls-independent vector). (2) dgate._companion builds the tested diffuse cue as comp[m] = shared_mag*base + cue_mag*Cd[m], where shared_mag*base (=5.831*base) is a SINGLE global cls-independent direction carrying ~100% of the masking energy and cue_mag*Cd[m] (=0.5) is the tiny per-member differentiating part. At alpha=1, mean-centering removes shared_mag*base EXACTLY (it IS the population common mode), leaving cue_mag*(Cd[m]-mean Cd[m]). So 100% of the diffuseness energy is, by construction, a removable common-mode offset -> floor~0 is mathematically guaranteed, independent of any learning. I confirmed numerically: pairwise_diff_dev ~1e-8 and ablated_max_sep=0 at all alpha. A diffuseness that is NOT a pure global common-mode leaves a real floor mean-centering cannot touch: (B) per-member structured masking noise noise_mag*N[m] has mean_m(N[m])~0, so global mean-centering removes ~none of it -> floor>0; (C) energy inside the differentiating subspace (big_mag*Cd[m], no common mode) has mean~0 -> mean-centering changes nothing -> floor unchanged. The ablation-invariance 'proof' (Step-0a) only establishes that constant subtraction injects no NEW differentiating signal (a tautology) and that an ablated common-mode-only cue stays signal-free; it does NOT show the transform recovers all diffuseness, and it does not test cls-dependent masking energy. Worse, the common-mode-ness is itself a PROBE SIMPLIFICATION: the deployed exp06 rig has R_coarse=5 (coarse-class structure, shared within a coarse class but differing across classes) and r_distractor=3 (distractor energy) folded into one global base; in the real rig coarse structure is not a global common mode and distractors may be per-member, so neither is removed by a single global mean-centering. The spec's own lock-2 names "diffuse-but-structured" as the NATIVE substrate and warns "never flatten to sharp" -- but the only diffuseness tested is the LEAST structured possible (a constant offset), and the structured case the spec says must be survived is exactly what was not tested.
lenses.verdict_reasoning: The refutation lands on the mechanism completely: floor~0 is a structural consequence of matching the re-posing (global mean-centering) to a construction that places 100% of masking energy in a single global common-mode offset. It is not evidence that "cue diffuseness is recoverable" in any general or even deployment-faithful sense. HOWEVER, the claim as written in the verdict does NOT over-generalize, because the artifact carries an explicit, accurate CUE_RECOVERABILITY_SCOPE note that says precisely what the refutation says: floor~0 is MEASURED for the common-mode-dominated construction, mean-centering recovers it BECAUSE the diffuseness is a removable common-mode offset, and generalization to non-common-mode/structured diffuseness is UNTESTED ("scopes cue recoverable to the construction, not a universal claim"). With that scope attached, the narrow claim survives: for THIS construction the floor genuinely is ~0 (off repose@1.0 floor 0.0136, 10 seeds, plateaued to 30000, ablation collapses to 0), and that is correctly reported as construction-scoped. The claim survives ONLY in its scoped form. It would NOT survive as a universal or deployment-faithful statement that the cue's diffuseness is recoverable. Severity is medium, not low, because two real gaps remain beyond the scope note: the fully_recoverable=true boolean is detached from the scope caveat in the JSON (carry-forward risk), and the scope note treats common-mode-dominance as a given property of the construction without flagging that it is a probe simplification of deployed structures (coarse-class R_coarse, distractor r_distractor) that are not globally common -- so the construction may not even be faithful to the "deployed" substrate it claims to characterize, and the spec's own stated native substrate (diffuse-but-structured) is the untested case.
required_caveats: Bind the scope to the number: irreducible_floor.fully_recoverable=true (and the intrinsic_inflated_split) must not be quoted without 'for the common-mode-dominated construction only; recovery is mathematically forced because the re-posing is global mean-centering matched to a pure global common-mode offset.' The boolean as it sits in the JSON is detached from CUE_RECOVERABILITY_SCOPE and is carry-forward-unsafe.

State that floor~0 is structurally forced, not discovered: the re-posing (comp - alpha*mu) is exactly global mean-centering and the tested cue puts ~100% of masking energy in a single cls-independent offset (shared_mag*base); so floor~0 follows from the construction independent of training. This is a near-tautology, not an empirical capability result.

Flag that the common-mode-ness is itself a probe simplification: the deployed exp06 rig's R_coarse (coarse-class, NOT globally shared) and r_distractor (possibly per-member) are folded into one global base. A single global mean-centering cannot remove per-coarse-class or per-member masking energy, so the deployed substrate's true floor may be >0. Faithfulness of the common-mode-dominated cue to the deployed rig is UNVERIFIED.

Note the ablation-invariance guard proves 'injects no new differentiating signal' (a tautology of constant subtraction), NOT 'recovers the diffuseness' and NOT 'content-blind in a capacity sense'. It does not test a cue with cls-dependent masking energy, so it provides no evidence the recovery generalizes.

Per the spec's own lock-2, diffuse-but-structured is the NATIVE substrate; the tested diffuseness (a constant offset) is the least-structured case. The two-part cue fix's 'irreducible floor' was measured ~0 only because the structured component that would create it was absent. Do not let 'floor~0' read as 'the cue needs no build-robust component'; the structured-diffuseness floor remains unmeasured.

lenses.refutation_attempt: The floor-equivalence verdict is ruler-dependent, and the SAME artifact publishes the contradicting ruler as its primary deliverable. Two distinct floor quantities live in exp07_interior_read.py: (1) own_sharp_floor = own_sharp - C (lines 104, 166), used ONLY by the LEGITIMACY block: off 0.0136, reshaped 0.0464, delta 0.033 -> floor_equivalent=True; (2) the _floor() function (lines 77-85) using a COMMON off-sharp ruler (1.1463 - C), used for the top-level CARD16.floors, irreducible_floor objects, and _topology(): off 0.0136, reshaped 0.1220, deployed 1.1463. Under (2), reshaped floor 0.122 exceeds the experiment's own MARGIN=0.10, is flagged fully_recoverable=False (raw 0.122 > 0.10), and _topology classifies CARD16 as klass='monotonic', min_regime='off' -- i.e. the experiment's own named deliverable (spec §3 'the topology') says the floor DOES order off below reshaped. So 'the cue floor does not select between them' is contradicted by the experiment's own published topology. Replacing the own ruler (reshaped-sharp 1.0707) with the common honest ruler (off-sharp 1.1463) gives reshaped floor 0.122 not 0.046 -> NOT floor-equivalent (delta 0.108 > 0.10). The verdict survives only by switching to own-sharp for off/reshaped while necessarily using common-sharp for the deployed column (whose own-sharp is dead=0) -- an internally inconsistent ruler within a single floors dict. Which ruler is honest? Spec §1 calls sharp 'the unreachable ruler / a measuring stick' and the spec §3 legitimacy clause asks for 'floor/ceiling/revival COMPARABLE' across columns, which argues FOR the common ruler the code already uses for deployed; the own-sharp reading launders the capacity gap out of the floor. Worse, the decomposition's load-bearing subtraction -- the sharp-gap (off-sharp - reshaped-sharp = 0.076) that is re-labeled 'uniform capacity cost' -- is NOT statistically robust: paired across the 10 seeds it is t=1.48 with a 5/5 sign split, so 'uniform offset cleanly removable from the floor' is asserted more than measured. The ceiling gap itself (0.108) IS robust (all 10 seeds off>reshaped, paired t=3.34, beyond the 2-sem band 0.082), so a capacity cost is real -- but its assignment to 'ceiling, not floor' is exactly the ruler choice under dispute, and equals (common-floor 0.122 - own-floor 0.046).
lenses.verdict_reasoning: The claim does not survive as stated. 'Floor-equivalent (both cue floors ~0)' is true ONLY under the own-sharp ruler used exclusively in the LEGITIMACY block; the experiment's primary floor deliverable -- the top-level CARD16.floors and the spec-§3 'topology' -- uses the common off-sharp ruler and reports reshaped floor 0.122 (vs off 0.0136), flagged not-fully-recoverable, with topology='monotonic' min='off'. Under that ruler the floor delta 0.108 exceeds the experiment's own equivalence MARGIN 0.10, so floor-equivalence fails by exp07's own threshold, and 'the floor does not select' is contradicted by exp07's own published topology classification. The verdict is internally inconsistent: it floors off/reshaped against their own sharps but is forced to floor deployed against the common off-sharp (own-sharp dead=0), mixing rulers in one floors dict. The blind-spot's common-ruler reading therefore holds. Mitigations that keep this at MEDIUM rather than HIGH: (a) the ceiling capacity gap is genuinely robust and seed-paired (t=3.34, 10/10), so SOMETHING real distinguishes the columns and the 'preserve on uniformity, at a measured ceiling cost' conclusion is defensible on the ceiling alone -- the error is in WHERE the cost is booked (floor vs ceiling/legitimacy), not in whether a cost exists; (b) at card-2 the two rulers AGREE (sharp gap 0.0003, ceiling gap 0.0026, both null), so the ruler ambiguity only bites at card-16, supporting the 'scale-growing' framing; (c) spec §3 line 210 ('each column carries its own sharp segment') does provide textual cover for own-sharp, so the choice is arguable, not fabricated. But the headline 'FLOOR-EQUIVALENT, floor does not select' must not be committed without disclosing that the experiment's own primary floor reading says the opposite. This is the 'caught != fixed' / 'motivated reasoning to reach preserve' pattern: the separation is defensible as a ceiling cost but is being smuggled past the floor by a ruler switch.
required_caveats: State plainly that floor-equivalence is RULER-DEPENDENT: it holds under own-sharp (delta 0.033) but FAILS under the common off-sharp ruler (delta 0.108 > MARGIN 0.10), and the common ruler is what the artifact's own top-level CARD16.floors, irreducible_floor (reshaped 0.122, fully_recoverable=False), and topology (monotonic, min=off) actually report.

Acknowledge the internal inconsistency: off/reshaped are floored against their own sharps in the LEGITIMACY block while deployed is necessarily floored against the common off-sharp; a single floors dict mixes two rulers. Pick one ruler and report the verdict consistently, or report both and let the reader see floor-equivalence flips.

Disclose that the sharp-gap (0.076) subtracted to make own-sharp floors equivalent (re-labeled 'uniform capacity cost') is NOT statistically significant at card-16 (paired t=1.48, 5/5 sign split); 'uniform offset cleanly removable from the floor' is overclaimed -- only the CEILING gap (0.108, paired t=3.34, 10/10) is robust.

Reframe the deliverable: the robust, defensible finding is a seed-paired ceiling capacity cost (off>reshaped by 0.108 at card-16, ~0 at card-2 -> scale-growing). Whether that cost is 'floor' or 'ceiling/legitimacy' is the ruler choice under dispute; do not present 'floor does not select' as a measured fact when the common-ruler topology selects off < reshaped.

Note the spec is genuinely ambiguous (§3 'each column carries its own sharp' vs §1 'unreachable ruler / measuring stick' vs §3 'floor/ceiling comparable'); the verdict should cite which spec reading it adopts and that the alternative reading reverses floor-equivalence, rather than silently adopting the one that yields preserve.

lenses.refutation_attempt:
I attacked all three sub-claims against the code and the 10-seed/30000 trajectories.

(1) Onset absoluteness — SURVIVES. exp07_core.PenaltySpec.lam12_at compares step against self.t1_step and self.t2_step (absolute ints), never a fraction. exp07_config PENALTY_REGIMES["reshaped"] pins t1_step=RESHAPED_T1_STEP=900 and t2_step=RESHAPED_T2_STEP=3600 as int(round(fraction*12000)). The reconfirm _pen overrides ONLY t2_step via onset_step(fraction)=fraction*12000, leaving t1 fixed at 900. Both onsets are genuinely budget-independent at the 30000 budget (the closed phase stays at a fixed 3600 steps; extending training adds post-clock differentiation, not a longer tie). This is a real fix of the fractional-onset drift confound. No refutation found.

(2) "Reconfirmed ceilings are plateaued" — REFUTED for one load-bearing cell. The off/repose@1.0 ceiling at card-16 (=1.1327, the off ceiling in the legitimacy gap) is NOT plateaued in substance: it rises monotonically every checkpoint (1.0318 -> 1.0672 -> 1.0913 -> 1.1327), the LAST segment delta is the LARGEST (+0.0414), and 6/10 seeds are still rising at 30000 with the biggest late gains (+0.206, +0.132, +0.109). It passes plateaued=true only because the criterion |delta last-2|<=0.05 is weak and 0.0414 squeaks under it — exactly the fixed-epsilon under-convergence trap the spec's own reconfirm lesson warns against (a rising-every-checkpoint, non-shrinking-delta curve is not at plateau). Contrast: reshaped@0.3/repose@1.0 is genuinely converged (last delta -0.0155, std collapsing 0.45->0.067, turning over) and ALL card-2 cells are flat. So the creep is a card-16-only under-convergence of the off-repose cell, not generic noise.

(3) "Off genuinely plateaued / gap is an off-not-converged artifact / gap could grow or shrink" — the gap IS partly an off-under-convergence artifact, but the direction REFUTES the worry's bite: off is rising while reshaped is flat, so the 0.1085 ceiling gap (and ceiling_worse=True / phasing-armed) would GROW with more training, i.e. the verdict UNDERSTATES the reshaped cost, never overstates it. Crucially the load-bearing conclusions do NOT use the creeping cell: (a) FLOOR-EQUIVALENT rests on own-sharp floors Fo,Fr, both anchored to ~flat sharps (off-creep only shrinks Fo toward 0 -> reinforces floor-equivalence); (b) the capacity-cost 0.0756 rests on off_sharp - resh_sharp, both flat -> robust; only delta_off_minus_reshaped_ceiling rests on the rising cell. So the off-creep does NOT threaten the legitimacy/floor/capacity numbers and if anything strengthens the "preserve carries a cost" lean.

(4) Fairness — equal-TRAINING is true (all cells same 30000 budget, same 10 seeds, same checkpoint), but the claim conflates equal-budget with equal-convergence: off-repose@16 is read while still rising, reshaped while converged. The phasing "preserve HOLDS" call (best reshaped @0.9=1.0758 >= off-0.10=1.0327) has only a ~0.043 cushion and would fail if off creeps ~2 more segments (off~1.215); reshaped onsets are themselves plateaued so cannot rise to compensate — a real but bounded fragility.
lenses.verdict_reasoning: The claim is mostly correct but overstated in one word. The two-clock onset is genuinely absolute and budget-independent in code (lam12_at vs absolute t1_step=900/t2_step=3600; reconfirm overrides only t2 via fraction*12000), so the fractional-onset drift confound is really fixed. The off-vs-reshaped comparison is equal-training (same budget/seeds/checkpoint) and the off-creep does NOT undermine the verdict: the creep runs UP while reshaped is flat, so it can only make the reshaped cost gap larger, and the load-bearing FLOOR-EQUIVALENT and capacity-cost numbers are anchored to the (flat) sharp references and own-sharp floors, not to the creeping off-repose cell. The off cue floor Fo even shrinks toward 0 under the creep, reinforcing floor-equivalence. So the central legitimacy conclusion survives a genuine refutation attempt. What does NOT survive verbatim is the blanket word "plateaued": the off/repose@1.0 card-16 ceiling is rising every checkpoint with a growing/largest final delta and 6/10 seeds still climbing, passing the plateau test only by a thin margin on a weak fixed-epsilon criterion — a substantively under-converged cell mislabeled plateaued=true. This is the exact under-convergence trap the spec itself flags. It is medium severity because it touches a load-bearing cell and a published number, but it cannot flip the call (wrong direction to help reshaped) and the dependent FLOOR/capacity numbers are insulated; the one place it bites is the ~0.043 phasing-recovery cushion, which is fragile but holds at current data.
required_caveats: off/repose@1.0 at card-16 (C=1.1327) is NOT substantively plateaued: it rises at every checkpoint (1.032/1.067/1.091/1.133), the final delta (+0.041) is the LARGEST, and 6/10 seeds are still climbing at 30000. It passes plateaued=true only by squeaking under the weak |delta last-2|<=0.05 criterion. Do not assert 'plateaued' unqualified — state 'off-repose@16 still creeping, plateau marginal' and prefer a shrinking-delta or 36000+ confirmation.

The 0.109 off-minus-reshaped ceiling gap is partly an off-under-convergence artifact, but the creep direction is UP, so the gap UNDERSTATES the reshaped capacity cost; report it as a lower bound that would GROW with more training, not as a converged value.

Distinguish equal-TRAINING (true: same 30000 budget, 10 seeds, checkpoint) from equal-CONVERGENCE (false: off-repose@16 read while rising, reshaped read converged). The 'fair' claim holds only at the budget level.

The phasing 'preserve HOLDS' recovery (best reshaped @0.9 = 1.0758 vs off-0.10 = 1.0327) has only a ~0.043 cushion against the off-creep and would fail if off creeps ~2 more segments; reshaped onsets are themselves plateaued and cannot rise to compensate. Flag this fragility.

The load-bearing FLOOR-EQUIVALENT and uniform-capacity-cost (0.0756) numbers are anchored to the ~flat sharp references / own-sharp floors and are robust to the off-creep; only the headline ceiling-gap / ceiling_worse / phasing-armed flag depend on the creeping cell. Keep this separation explicit so the off-creep is not used to discredit the robust deliverables.

lenses.refutation_attempt:
The claim "topology = monotonic (off<=reshaped<<deployed) and INVARIANT across cardinality -> member-count is a non-lever / topology is not a cardinality effect" does not survive as worded, for three connected reasons grounded in the artifacts.

(1) "Monotonic" is a near-degenerate label, not a structural finding. The deployed column is uniformly dead (C=0 at both cards; deployed revives=False), and the floor formula is floor=ruler-C with a COMMON off-sharp ruler (exp07_interior_read.py _floor, lines 77-85). So the deployed floor is mechanically pinned to the ruler itself (CARD16: ruler 1.1463 == deployed floor 1.1463; CARD2: 1.3822 == 1.3822). The code comment (lines 80-81) admits this: the dead column "reads a MAXIMAL floor". Consequence: deployed always supplies the spread max; spread is ~1.13/1.38 >> margin 0.10, so `separable` is structurally unreachable; the min is always off or reshaped. The classifier therefore collapses to exactly one live bit: monotonic iff reshaped_floor>=off_floor, sweet-spot@reshaped iff reshaped_floor<off_floor. "Both monotonic" thus means only "reshaped did not undershoot off." The 100%-of-spread driver (deployed-is-dead) is just exp06's already-known OR-kill, re-measured, not a new cue x penalty topology.

(2) The part that actually matters -- the off-vs-reshaped relationship, which is the spec's OWN second gate condition for declaring invariance (§1: "OR-kill holds AND the reshaped-vs-off relationship holds") -- is scale-DEPENDENT, not invariant. Computed from the reconfirmed ceilings: card-2 off_C-reshaped_C=+0.0027 (z=0.03, a dead tie), but card-16 off_C-reshaped_C=+0.1085 (z=2.64, a significant gap). The verdict's own LEGITIMACY block records this: uniform_capacity_cost_card2=0.0003, uniform_capacity_cost_card16=0.0756, capacity_cost_scale_growing=True, ceiling_worse=True. So a real cost appears at card-16 that is absent at card-2 -- a monotone-with-cardinality trend over the two points. That is precisely a member-count effect on the reshaped-vs-off relationship, in tension with "member-count is a non-lever."

(3) TOPOLOGY_INVARIANT_16_vs_2=True is computed by string-comparing the coarse klass label only (line 152), a statistic that is BLIND to (2): monotonic fires whenever off<=reshaped, which is true at both cards regardless of whether reshaped ties off (card-2) or pays a significant cost (card-16). So the reported invariance captures only the trivial deployed-dead part and the sign of off<=reshaped; it cannot see the scale-growing gap that the same JSON records elsewhere. Two cardinalities also cannot establish invariance of a relationship that is itself changing between those two points -- and card-2's large SEM (~0.07-0.10) swamps its own +0.003 delta, so card-2 cannot even confirm the equivalence robustly. A third cardinality would be needed to claim invariance or to distinguish the trend from noise.

What I could NOT refute (fairness): the OR-kill (deployed dead; off/reshaped alive at sharp) genuinely replicates at both cardinalities, and off<=reshaped (floor sense) holds at both. The verdict is also honest -- it does NOT assert reshaped==off uniformly; it explicitly flags the scale-growing capacity cost. So the WEAK reading ("OR-kill / deployed-dead structure replicates; member-count does not flip liveness") survives. The STRONG reading in the claim ("topology invariant -> member-count is a non-lever / not a cardinality effect") does not.
lenses.verdict_reasoning: The claim as worded overstates the evidence. The "invariant" half rests on a klass-string match that is structurally near-forced: with the deployed column uniformly dead, the common-ruler floor pins deployed to the maximum, makes `separable` unreachable, and reduces the topology to a single bit (reshaped vs off ordering) whose informative content is dominated 100% by the trivial exp06-known deployed-dead jump. The discriminating off-vs-reshaped part -- the spec's own second gate condition and the only non-trivial content -- is NOT invariant: it is a dead tie at card-2 (z=0.03) but a significant, scale-growing capacity cost at card-16 (z=2.64), as the verdict's own LEGITIMACY block records (capacity_cost_scale_growing=True, ceiling_worse=True). That is a member-count effect on the reshaped channel, directly undercutting "member-count is a non-lever." TOPOLOGY_INVARIANT=True is computed only on the coarse label and is blind to this. Two cardinality points cannot anchor an invariance claim about a relationship that visibly changes between them, especially with card-2's SEM larger than its own delta. Severity is medium, not high: the conclusion that actually flows downstream into the design (deployed-dead OR-kill replicates; liveness is not member-count-gated; reshaped never undershoots off) does survive, and the verdict text is internally honest about the scale-growing cost -- the failure is one of over-claimed wording ("non-lever / not a cardinality effect") rather than a wrong measurement. The fix is caveat-level, not a re-run.
required_caveats: Restrict the wording: replace 'member-count is a non-lever / topology is not a cardinality effect' with 'the OR-kill (deployed-dead) structure and the off<=reshaped ordering replicate at 2 and 16; member-count does not flip liveness'. The stronger non-lever claim is not supported.

State explicitly that the deployed floor is mechanically pinned to the off-sharp ruler (deployed C=0 -> floor=ruler), so deployed-dead supplies ~100% of the spread at both cards; 'monotonic' therefore reduces to the single bit 'reshaped did not undershoot off' and 'separable' is structurally unreachable in this construction.

Disclose that the discriminating off-vs-reshaped relationship is NOT cardinality-invariant: floor-equivalent at card-2 (off_C-reshaped_C=+0.003, z~0.03) but a significant, scale-growing capacity cost at card-16 (+0.108, z~2.64); this is the verdict's own capacity_cost_scale_growing=True / ceiling_worse=True and is a member-count effect on the reshaped channel.

Note that TOPOLOGY_INVARIANT=True is a coarse klass-string comparison (interior_read line 152) that is blind to the scale-growing off-reshaped gap; invariance was tested on the label, not on the quantity that matters.

Flag the two-point limitation: invariance of a relationship that changes between the only two sampled cardinalities cannot be established from 2 points; card-2's SEM (~0.07-0.10) exceeds its own off-reshaped delta, so even the card-2 equivalence is weakly supported. A third cardinality is needed to claim invariance or to separate trend from noise.

Scope the finding to the common-mode-dominated cue construction (already noted in CUE_RECOVERABILITY_SCOPE) -- the floors and ordering are measured for this specific diffuse-cue structure, not a universal cue-floor topology.
